Good! The regex is mostly working, but there's one issue: it's matching 2024-02-30 which is invalid (February doesn't have 30 days). The requirement says "Assume that February can have up to 29 days in all years, without distinguishing leap years from non-leap years." This means February should only allow days 01-29, not 30 or 31.

Let me refine the date pattern to handle February specially:
steps.command:

import re

# Test different date patterns
test_dates = [
    "2024-01-31",  # Valid (Jan has 31)
    "2024-02-29",  # Valid (Feb can have up to 29)
    "2024-02-30",  # Invalid (Feb max 29)
    "2024-04-30",  # Valid (Apr has 30)
    "2024-04-31",  # Invalid (Apr has 30)
]

# Date pattern that handles Feb specially:
# Jan (01): 01-31
# Feb (02): 01-29
# Mar (03): 01-31
# Apr (04): 01-30
# May (05): 01-31
# Jun (06): 01-30
# Jul (07): 01-31
# Aug (08): 01-31
# Sep (09): 01-30
# Oct (10): 01-31
# Nov (11): 01-30
# Dec (12): 01-31

# Better approach: use alternation
# (0[13578]|1[02]): months with 31 days (01, 03, 05, 07, 08, 10, 12)
# (0[469]|11): months with 30 days (04, 06, 09, 11)
# 02: February with 01-29

pattern = r'\b(?:(?:0[13578]|1[02])-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])|(?:0[469]|11)-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|30)|02-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]))\b'

# Wait, this doesn't include the year. Let me create a complete pattern:
pattern2 = r'\b(?:[0-9]{4})-(?:(?:0[13578]|1[02])-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])|(?:0[469]|11)-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|30)|02-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]))\b'

for date in test_dates:
    if re.search(pattern2, date):
        print(f"{date}: MATCH")
    else:
        print(f"{date}: NO MATCH")

EOF
